substantive_reconstruction.common_action_inclusion: For Q_pi acting by factor permutation and any one endomorphism X, both Q_pi X^tensor(n) and X^tensor(n)Q_pi send a pure tensor to the same list of X-transformed vectors in permuted order. Pure tensors span V^tensor(n), so the equality holds on the full space. In particular it holds for every g∈GL(V), proving the actual defined B⊆A'. The same g acts in every factor; neither 'diagonal matrix' nor merely unitary g is substituted. This directly discharges rubric1 and step1 instead of relying on the narrower sentence in the source.
substantive_reconstruction.interpolation_and_singular_generators: The question supplies A'=span{X^tensor(n):X∈End(V)}, so the remaining task is genuinely every X, including singular X. When d>0, det(X+tI) is monic of degree d; its finite root set leaves n+1 distinct complex sample points. F(t)=(X+tI)^tensor(n) is an operator-valued polynomial of degree at most n, by expansion over which of the n factors contributes tI. The candidate's Lagrange coefficients have nonzero denominators at distinct samples and reconstruct F(0)=sum_j ell_j(0)F(t_j). Each sample uses an invertible X+t_jI and therefore belongs to the GL-defined B, with no unitarity claim; linearity then puts X^tensor(n) in B. This verifies rubric2–4 and steps2–4. No coefficient-degree equality or d≥n premise is necessary.
substantive_reconstruction.bicommutant_and_boundaries: A is the image span of the finite permutation group: it contains the identity, is closed under products and, for the canonical inner product on(C^d)^tensor(n), satisfies Q_pi†=Q_(pi^-1). It is thus a finite-dimensional unital star algebra, so its bicommutant equals A. Once B=A' has been proved, B'=A''=A follows; the theorem is not applied to an arbitrary non-self-adjoint subalgebra. At n=0 the tensor unit is C, all zeroth tensor powers are1, both algebras are C and one interpolation sample suffices. At d=0,n>0 the ambient tensor power and End algebra are zero, so both commutants within that algebra and both spans are zero. The n=0,d=0 case is covered by the tensor-unit branch, not incorrectly treated as zero. These checks justify rubric5/step5, including nonfaithful permutation actions when d<n.
